chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sufyan ibn Ibrahim al-Jariri, from al-Harith ibn al-Haseera al-Asadi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I entered with my father to the Ka'bah, and he prayed upon the red marble slab between the two pillars. He said: 'In this place, the people made a pact: if the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) dies or is killed, they will not return this command (leadership) to anyone from his Household ever.' I said, 'And who were they?' He said: 'The first one, and the second one, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and Salim ibn al-Habibah.'
ai.seo_question: Who were the companions that pacted to exclude the Ahl al-Bayt from leadership according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the specific spot in the Ka'bah where the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) pledged to exclude the Ahl al-Bayt from leadership upon his death, a pivotal event in the succession narrative. He explicitly names Abu Bakr, Umar, Abu Ubaydah, and Salim as the key figures in this pact, providing a concise Shia perspective on the immediate post-Prophetic political consolidation. This narration underscores the Shia view that the exclusion of the Prophet's Household was a deliberate, pre-arranged decision rather than a spontaneous occurrence.
